items.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15
items.q: Do you remember Buddy Petit? Oh yeah, sure. I played with Buddy Petit.

ctx.x: But after I got from this Christian organization, then I had to have everything correct, you see. Yeah. Yeah.

So I went down to the Catholic Church. I was born to the Catholic Church. I went down there, and I got my boy's sister, and I was surprised. And I always owned the impression that I was born with Marshall Levin, or the first. But when I look on that verse, it was Marshall Levin. Marshall Levin. Mm. Marshall Levin, 1897. My dad was a musician too. Oh, was he? Yeah. He used to play guitar, bandolin, bass. What was his name? Henry, Renny. He was working for a lot of war lines when they was on Burgundy Street. That's…

items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-04-07
items.q: I've seen Buddy Petit, but the first one played, you know, with his derby.

ctx.x: of course, they didn't want to give me the credit. I didn't want it, no, huh? Because all I was trying to do, take the ideas, you know, to get ahead of the other fella. I went to the, this must have been back in 1910 or 11, but way back then, got a coconut shell and cut it in half. Because you see, I've seen Buddy Petit, but the first one played, you know, with his derby. He was the first man ever played with a derby, you see, and him and another fella, Frederick Kepage, you all heard talking about Frederick…
